❇️ Head of the Reformists Front of Gilan Province: Reviving the Islamabad Agreement must become the organizational priority of the Reformists Front

🔺 Saharkhiz, Head of the Reformists Front of Gilan Province, stressing the need for the Reformists Front to play its organizational role under the country's sensitive conditions, proposed that reviving the Islamabad Agreement and preventing the country from sliding back into a state of war be placed on the agenda as the main focus of this organization's activities until further notice.

▪️ At the joint meeting of the Committee on Provincial Affairs of the Reformists Front of Iran with the presiding boards of the provincial reformist fronts, he proposed that speeches and meetings related to the issue of peace and the Islamabad Agreement be held across the country with greater speed, with the participation of all reformists—both members active in organizational meetings and other forces of this movement.

▪️ Saharkhiz also identified the launch of an online campaign in support of the Islamabad Agreement as another necessary step, expressing hope that it would be widely welcomed by a people weary of war.

▪️ The Head of the Reformists Front of Gilan Province, referring to the media capacity of reformists in the provinces, stressed the need to centrally activate news outlets and media close to this movement, and called on the public relations and media committee of the Reformists Front of Iran to play a more effective role in coordinating these capacities.

▪️ In conclusion, he stressed the need to plan for utilizing the organizational and media capacities of reformists in support of peace and agreement.

🔹 The Reformists Front of Iran's address on social networks: Telegram, Instagram, X (Twitter)

❇️ Vice Chairman of the Kurdistan Reform Front: The Islamabad Agreement is an opportunity to reduce tension and sustain diplomacy🔺Ramezan Yousefi, Vice Chairman of the Reform Front of Kurdistan Province, stressing the need to support the Islamabad Agreement between Iran and the US, called peace a wise choice for safeguarding people's lives, the calm of society, and the country's future, and called for the government's cooperation with provincial reform fronts to hold support conferences.▪️Yousefi, stating that peace is neither a sign of weakness nor a means of disregarding the rights of the nation, said: The Islamabad Agreement is an opportunity to reduce tension and continue the path of diplomacy, and supporting it amounts to supporting calm and national interests.▪️Referring to the responsibility of senior government officials in the provinces, he also emphasized: Governors must, recognizing the sensitivity of the situation, direct their words and conduct toward public calm and solidarity. Certain stances or expressions of solidarity with warmongers may create the impression of alignment with opponents of the agreement and supporters of confrontation—an impression that, even if unintended, merits reflection.▪️The Vice Chairman of the Reform Front of Kurdistan Province, stressing that officials' responsibility is not limited to administering affairs, added: Safeguarding people's hope and refraining from fueling unrest are also among officials' important responsibilities.▪️In conclusion, Yousefi called for a government directive to governors to engage and cooperate with provincial reform fronts in holding appropriate conferences with maximum attendance, so as to pave the way for declaring the support and solidarity of the broader society with the government's policies on the path to peace, and for explaining the achievements of the Islamabad Agreement for the country and the people.🔹The Iran Reform Front's address on social networks: Telegram, Instagram, X (Twitter)

Interviews and explanatory content can also help strengthen this movement in the virtual space.▪️The Head of the Reform Front of Fars Province also stressed the need for coordination with provincial officials and said: We can hold conversations with governors and their political deputies to create the ground for holding meetings attended by reformist and principlist parties. Inviting moderate and knowledgeable principlist figures to participate in this movement can also help expand the social reach of the campaign and strengthen the message of peace.🔹The Iran Reform Front's addresses on social networks: Telegram, Instagram, X (Twitter)

❇️ Head of the Reform Front of Hormozgan Province: Support for the agreement must be carried out with the participation of all pillars of the government and political currents

🔺 Mohammad Zakeri, Head of the Reform Front of Hormozgan Province, emphasizing the importance of the Islamabad Agreement, said: Without a doubt, this agreement is a great and unprecedented step that is the result of sacrifices, courage, and political and social efforts made in the country.

▪️ Referring to the need to avoid politicizing this movement, he stated: In order for support for the agreement to bear fruit, the pillars of the government must first clarify their position, and governance institutions and principled figures who agree with this path must also step forward. Governors must also play a role in this process so that the ground is prepared for synergy among different sectors.

▪️ Zakeri added: If only the Reform Front is to take the lead and the main burden of this movement falls on the shoulders of the reformists, the work will not reach the desired result and the movement will remain incomplete. Given the unfavorable conditions of many provinces and the costs that gathering forces entails, it is necessary that this action begin at the level of the government and the pillars of governance and then expand in the provinces.

▪️ The Head of the Reform Front of Hormozgan Province proposed that before entering into field actions, the capacity for support of the agreement in cyberspace should be measured and the level of public reception should be evaluated, so that if the ground is prepared, executive and field plans can be pursued with stronger backing.

🔹 Address of the Iran Reform Front on social networks: Telegram, Instagram, X (Twitter)
